emittedWhyItMatters: The supplied governed record's action level is defined as an 8-hour TWA dose, not an instantaneous reading. If the TWA equals or exceeds 85 dBA, the hearing conservation programme requirement is triggered and hearing protection, monitoring and signage become required controls. If the TWA is below 85 dBA (e.g., the setter is only briefly at that position or the press cycles intermittently), the action level is not met and the programme is not currently required on these facts. The single reading alone cannot resolve which of these applies.
explanationSummary: A single instantaneous 88 dBA reading was taken at the setter's ear during press cycling, but the supplied governed record measures the hearing conservation action level as an 8-hour time-weighted average dose, and the observation itself notes no duration or dosimetry data was captured to make that comparison — so whether the action level is actually triggered remains open. Separately, and regardless of that open question, the observation establishes as a current fact that no hearing protection is worn and no zoning signage is posted at this position. The determination of programme applicability should not proceed on the single reading alone; a shift-representative TWA or dosimetry result is needed to settle it.
